chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid Al-Hariri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever is ascetic in the world, Allah will establish wisdom in his heart, and make his tongue speak with it, and give him insight into the faults of the world—its ailment and its cure—and He will bring him out of the world safe and sound into the House of Peace.

key_terms.دَارِ السَّلَامِ: The House of Peace (a term for Paradise or the afterlife)
key_terms.زَهِدَ: To be ascetic or renounce worldly desires

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of being ascetic in the world according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links *zuhd* (asceticism) not merely to renunciation, but to the divine bestowal of *hikmah* (wisdom) and *basirah* (insight). This spiritual purification ensures the believer navigates the world's trials with clarity, ultimately transitioning safely to the *Dar al-Salam* (Abode of Peace), a concept central to Shia eschatology.
